VETERANS AFFAIRS COMMISSION MINUTES
  WEDNESDAY, NOVEMBER 13, 2024
  2525 GRAND AVENUE
  ROOM 204, 5:00 PM

Juanita Doplemore, Chair  Victor Hill, Commissioner
Kenneth Osborn, Vice Chair  James Schotter, Commissioner
Antawnette Atkins Blade, Commissioner  Nicholas Sramek, Commissioner
James Goodin, Commissioner

  FINISHED AGENDA & DRAFT MINUTES

  SPECIAL MEETING

CALL TO ORDER

Chair Doplemore called the meeting to order at 5:09 p.m.

ROLL CALL

Commissioners Present: Goodin, Osborn, Doplemore, Sramek, Schotter

Commissioners Absent: Hill, Atkins Blade

Also present: Gina Overholt, Coordinator.

Also in attendance: Dick Caley, Steve Hageman, Daren Hendon, Jesse Soria, Christina White (VA
Long Beach Health Care System), Christina Boatwright

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

Commissioner Sramek led the Pledge of Allegiance.

REGULAR AGENDA

1.  24-55585  Recommendation to approve the minutes for the Veterans Affairs Commission
  meeting of Wednesday, October 16, 2024.

  A motion was made by Commissioner Sramek, seconded by Commissioner
  Schotter, to approve recommendation. The motion carried by the following
  vote:

  Yes:  5  Goodin, Osborn, Doplemore, Sramek, Schotter
  No:  0  None
  Recused: 0  None
  Abstain: 0  None
  Absent: 2  Hill, Atkins Blade

  Page 1 of 4
   VETERANS AFFAIRS COMMISSION MINUTES
  WEDNESDAY, NOVEMBER 13, 2024
  2525 GRAND AVENUE
  ROOM 204, 5:00 PM

2.  24-55586  Recommendation to discuss presentation on potential VASH/Veterans Housing
  Project in Cambodia Town.

  A motion was made by Commissioner Osborn, seconded by Commissioner
  Sramek, to approve recommendation to receive and file. The
  motion carried by the following vote:

  Yes:  5  Goodin, Osborn, Doplemore, Sramek, Schotter
  No:  0  None
  Recused: 0  None
  Abstain: 0  None
  Absent: 2  Hill, Atkins Blade

  Three representatives of the proposed 1400 Cherry development, Dick Caley (with
  Coastal Equities), Steve Hageman and Daren Hendon (with Veterans Social
  Services, Inc.) presented on the project. 1400 Cherry is envisioned as an 11-story,
  100-unit affordable housing development that is also a Veteran-focused facility,
  offering Veterans in-need residential care, case management and onsite social
  services. A robust discussion followed the presentation.

3.  24-55587  Recommendation to discuss new Housing-Related Subcommittee.

  A Laid Over was made by Commissioner Schotter, seconded by
  Commissioner Doplemore, Laid Over. The motion carried by the following
  vote:

  Yes:  5  Goodin, Osborn, Doplemore, Sramek, Schotter
  No:  0  None
  Recused: 0  None
  Abstain: 0  None
  Absent: 2  Hill, Atkins Blade

4.  24-55588  Recommendation to discuss 2024 Veterans Day Celebration.

  Staff liaison Overholt thanked the Commission for their support of a successful
  Veterans Day Celebration. Commissioners discussed the great turn out for the
  event, the excellent opportunity drawing items, the things that worked well, and
  potential areas for improvement.

  A motion was made by Commissioner Schotter, seconded by Commissioner
  Sramek, to approve recommendation to receive and file. The
  motion carried by the following vote:

  Yes:  5 Goodin, Osborn, Doplemore, Sramek, Schotter
  No:  0 None

  Page 2 of 4

  2525 GRAND AVENUE

  Recused: 0 None
  Abstain: 0 None
  Absent: 2 Hill, Atkins Blade

5.  24-55589  Recommendation to discuss Veterans Banner Program.

  A motion was made by Commissioner Goodin, seconded by Commissioner
  Schotter, to approve recommendation to receive and file. The
  motion carried by the following vote:

  Yes:  5  Goodin, Osborn, Doplemore, Sramek, Schotter
  No:  0  None
  Recused: 0  None
  Abstain: 0  None
  Absent: 2  Hill, Atkins Blade

  Chair Osborn reported on the subcommittee meeting. Collaboration between the
  subcommittee and the City is essential to a smooth running program. Staff liaison
  Overholt set the next subcommittee meeting to discuss lessons learned, the project
  timeline and selection criteria for Monday, 11/18, at 3 p.m. Commissioners Osborn,
  Doplemore, AtkinsBlade, Goodin and former Commissioner Smith will be included.

6.  24-55590  Recommendation to discuss End-of-Year Celebration on December 11.

  A motion was made by Commissioner Schotter, seconded by Commissioner
  Goodin, to approve recommendation to receive and file. The
  motion carried by the following vote:

  Yes:  5  Goodin, Osborn, Doplemore, Sramek, Schotter
  No:  0  None
  Recused: 0  None
  Abstain: 0  None
  Absent: 2  Hill, Atkins Blade

  The end-of-year celebration will either take place at the RAHEC or another location
  (a non-City facility), but still be open to the public. A potluck sign-up sheet was
  distributed. Discussion about the celebration details will continue offline.

7.  24-55592  Recommendation to discuss Leadership Elections.

  A substitute motion was made by Commissioner Osborn, seconded by
  Commissioner Doplemore, Substitute Motion to add a secretary position to
  the executive board in the knowledge that the role and responsibilities still
  need to be defined. The motion carried by the following vote:

  Page 3 of 4
   VETERANS AFFAIRS COMMISSION MINUTES
  WEDNESDAY, NOVEMBER 13, 2024
  2525 GRAND AVENUE
  ROOM 204, 5:00 PM

  Yes:  5  Goodin, Osborn, Doplemore, Sramek, Schotter
  No:  0  None
  Recused: 0  None
  Abstain: 0  None
  Absent: 2  Hill, Atkins Blade

  Chair and Vice Chair elections will be held at the December’s meeting.
  Commissioners interested in these positions can E-mail staff liaison Overholt.
  Nominations will also be accepted at the meeting. Overholt shared a a slide about
  these roles from the Commissioner handbook.

PUBLIC COMMENT

Guest Christina White suggested that badges be “bank teller” style with name only and no photo.

ANNOUNCEMENTS

CD 5 Councilmember Kerr is sponsoring a Veterans Donation drive from November 11 to December
27, with drop off locations throughout the City. Commissioner Goodin suggested that the Commission
have magnetic name tags to identify them at City functions.

ADJOURNMENT

Chair Doplemore adjourned the meeting at 6:53 p.m.
